chunks: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Yusuf ibn Zariq al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Anbasa, the freedman of Al-Rashid, narrated to me, saying: Darim ibn Qabaysa ibn Nahshal ibn Majma al-Nahsheli al-Sa'eh in Sarman narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) narrated to us from his father, from his forefather, from Ali, from his forefather, from Ali (peace be upon him) from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

He said: Do good to those who deserve it and to those who do not deserve it. If the one to whom you do good deserves it, then he is the one who deserves it; and if he does not deserve it, then you are the one who deserves it.

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: Those who deserve it / The worthy ones
key_terms.غَيْرِ أَهْلِهِ: Those who do not deserve it / The unworthy ones

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of doing good to those who do not deserve it in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the Imams from the Prophet, emphasizes the proactive nature of *al-ma'ruf* (goodness) in Shia ethics, where the doer becomes the 'worthy' party by virtue of their intention and action, regardless of the recipient's merit. It underscores the concept of *ihsan* (excellence) in social relations, encouraging believers to bestow kindness universally to cultivate personal virtue and social cohesion. The teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on the moral agency of the individual in creating value through benevolent acts.
